Generative AI · Model training · Deployment

PlotCraft

From a natural-language instruction to executable scientific-figure code—and a public application to try it.

The problem

Generating a scientific figure involves more than producing an image: the underlying plotting code should execute and remain editable. PlotCraft turns text instructions into Python/Matplotlib code that users can review, render, and reuse.

What I built

I developed the end-to-end system: prepared the filtered PYVEC dataset of 53,846 examples, built the training pipeline, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B with LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO, and deployed the resulting application on Hugging Face ZeroGPU.

I also built a containerized FastAPI service, configuration and error handling, health checks, automated tests, and GitHub Actions workflows for validation, Docker builds, and deployment.

Engineering decisions

  • Executable output: return Python/Matplotlib code so users can inspect and modify a figure.
  • Training sequence: follow supervised fine-tuning with GRPO reinforcement learning.
  • Browser-based rendering: execute the preview in an isolated browser worker with execution limits, keeping generated code off the application server.
  • Reproducible delivery: package the API with Docker and use automated tests and CI/CD to validate changes.

Result & evaluation

97.0% internal code-execution rate after GRPO

This measures whether code executed in the internal evaluation. It does not establish visual quality, scientific correctness, or performance on an independent benchmark.

The deployed application makes the system inspectable: enter a prompt, review generated code, render a preview, and copy the code.

What this demonstrates

Work across the complete model lifecycle: data preparation, fine-tuning, evaluation, model serving, execution boundaries, testing, and deployment.
